title: AI-Enabled Wake Scheduling for FR3 Ultra-Massive MIMO IoT Devices: A Simulated Traffic and Beam-Sweep-Aware Benchmark
content: This paper presents two related benchmark studies of artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled wake scheduling for ultra-low-power devices in Frequency Range 3 (FR3, 7–24 GHz) ultra-massive multiple-input multiple-output (UM-MIMO) Internet of Things (IoT) networks, evaluated as Pareto-frontier trade-offs between energy and access performance. Study 1 benchmarks wake scheduling for narrowband IoT (NB-IoT) devices under simulated bursty traffic, comparing a classical fixed-interval policy, a genie-aided policy with perfect intensity knowledge, and a learned traffic-intensity estimator, and characterizes the energy–latency frontier together with tail (95th-percentile) latency. Study 2 addresses beam-sweep-aware wake scheduling, in which an idle-mode UM-MIMO IoT device must also account for directional beam-sweep paging overhead, and evaluates listen-window policies against a learned arrival-time predictor on an energy–reliability frontier. In both studies, learned, time-varying state estimates did not uniformly improve on well-designed fixed-policy baselines. They helped in specific regimes, substantially reducing tail latency relative to the genie-aided reference in Study 1 and uniquely reaching near-perfect paging reliability in Study 2, whereas simple classical policies remained preferable elsewhere. The mechanism behind each gain differed between the two problems, indicating that gains from learned prediction are regime- and context-dependent rather than universal.
